clue.text: Cutback disturbs southern firm making plaster coating

indicators.note: to disturb is to break in on, so one piece barges into the middle of the others

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm
split after its third letter, this one clue word becomes a reversal instruction applied to its own first three letters

explanation.surface: A company in the south is hit by budget cuts while working on plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' looks like a noun meaning a saving, but splits in two: its first three letters, turned back, go inside S and CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat and decorate walls.

clue.text: Men put flagging energy into this signal achievement

definitions.text: Men put flagging energy into this signal achievement

parts.words: Men put flagging energy into this signal achievement
parts.note: flagging seems to mean tiring, but here it is waving flags: a system of signalling where men hold flags in set positions

explanation.surface: Weary men still manage a notable feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flagging' and 'signal' both play double: tiring and notable on the surface, flag-waving and signalling underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a signalling system using hand-held flags in different arm positions.

clue.text: A hunter arranged to expose fox thus

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A huntsman organises digging out a fox from its hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes UNEARTH from the letters of A HUNTER; a fox's den is its earth, so to dig it out is to expose it this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox lives in an earth, so driving or digging it out of there is to unearth it.

clue.text: Become angry and destroy preliminary sketch

parts.note: to cut up a thing is to destroy it by slicing it apart
a rough is an artist's first draft or outline drawing

explanation.surface: An artist loses their temper and tears up the first draft.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to turn nasty or show temper.

clue.text: A French leader, articulate and prosperous

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so the first letter of French is taken

parts.note: articulate means able to speak fluently and clearly

explanation.surface: A French head of state is eloquent and well off.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent is a synonym of wealthy or well-to-do.

clue.text: Standard support required by runners-up

parts.note: a standard is a flag, and the pole holding it is what you need to run a flag up

explanation.surface: Second-place finishers need the usual backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as normal and 'runners-up' as also-rans, but a standard is a flag and runners-up are people hoisting one.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the pole that holds up a flag.

clue.text: High-flyer's harmless piece of mischief

definitions.meaning: a songbird famous for singing as it soars
a prank or bit of fun done for amusement

explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a soaring songbird, and a lark is also a playful escapade.

clue.text: Half of them plead for a ruler

indicators.note: half of means one of the two halves of the word is taken, here its back two letters

parts.note: to press for something is to urge or plead for it

explanation.surface: Half the crowd beg for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes the back half of THEM, EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign, so a ruler.

clue.text: Shrub once belonging to you and me

parts.note: thy is the old-fashioned word for your
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bush that used to be owned by the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a small woody aromatic plant, a low shrub used as a herb.

clue.text: Trip south from head of river

indicators.note: taking something from the head of a word means it comes off the front

parts.note: the Stour is a river in southern England

explanation.surface: A journey going south from a river's source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of river' looks like a source or an R, but means the front of a river's name: S comes off STOUR, a river in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey or excursion, a trip.

clue.text: Era most chaotic for this virtuoso

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The most disordered age produced this great performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' rearranges ERA MOST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master musician, a virtuoso performer or conductor.

clue.text: Be a waster, yet work hard in a test

indicators.note: in means the work-and-hard pair sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a try is a test or attempt
OP, short for opus, is a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Be idle, though you have to slog in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be a waster' suggests a layabout but means to waste away; the indicator 'in' puts work and hard inside a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to waste away, as an unused muscle withers.

clue.text: A page put into a sharper version?

definitions.text: A page put into a sharper version?

indicators.note: put into means the first pair of pieces is placed inside the rearranged letters
a version is a different rendering, so the letters are rendered anew

explanation.surface: A page of text is reworked into a crisper form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges A SHARPER into PARHRASE, and 'put into' places A P after its third letter. The whole clue also describes the answer: restating a page more sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrasing is rewording a passage, ideally more clearly, into a new version.

clue.text: Hand over church keys

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
D and E are two musical keys

explanation.surface: A vicar surrenders the church keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' looks like door keys but means two musical keys, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or give up possession, as territory.

clue.text: Peacekeepers turning offensive

parts.note: the UN (United Nations) supplies peacekeeping forces
turning, as in turning red, means becoming

explanation.surface: Soldiers keeping the peace go on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an attack in a military surface, but means improper or unseemly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbecoming behaviour is unseemly and improper, hence objectionable.

clue.text: Colours hard to mix left out of some pigment

indicators.note: to mix means the letters are blended into a new order
left out says the letter for left is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Colours are tricky to blend when a pigment is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from COLOURS; 'to mix' jumbles what is left with H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochrous means of or like ochre, an earthy yellow-brown pigment.

clue.text: Docker giving fellow notes before me

parts.note: Steve is any man's name, so a fellow
in the sol-fa scale do and re are the notes that come before mi, also written me

explanation.surface: A dock worker passes a man some notes before handing them on to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the third note of the sol-fa scale, so the notes before it are DO and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, a dock worker.

clue.text: Failure to recall first-class nurse with degree rebounded

indicators.note: rebounded means bounced back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class
SEN stands for State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade
MA is Master of Arts, a degree

explanation.surface: A top nurse with a degree forgets everything after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebounded' turns the whole run AI SEN MA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, an inability to remember.

clue.text: Big guns indisposed to be seen in the bloody Tube

indicators.note: to be seen in means one piece appears inside another

parts.note: an artery is a tube carrying blood
indisposed means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Important people are too unwell to be spotted on the wretched London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bloody Tube' looks like a curse on London's Underground railway, but means a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is heavy guns, so big guns.

clue.text: Head of English takes hint about record of poem

indicators.note: the head is the top, so the first letter of English is taken
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt
a log is a written record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: An English department head takes a tip about the record of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, often a dialogue between shepherds.

clue.text: Serving American in pub is sensible

indicators.note: in means the soldier is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a local is a person's neighbourhood pub
a GI is an American soldier, one serving in the forces

explanation.surface: Working as an American in a pub is a sound decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' suggests bar work in a pub but means serving in the military; a LOCAL is a British word for a regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical reasoning is rational and sound, hence sensible.

clue.text: Bondsman turned back by the disastrous flood

indicators.note: turned back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a serf was a man bound to the land, a bondsman

indicators.note: disastrous suggests ruin, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A slave is driven back by a catastrophic flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses SERF to FRES; 'disastrous' jumbles THE into HET.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshet is a sudden rush of fresh water into a river, a flood.

clue.text: Way in which new dictionary covered "square dance"

indicators.note: covered means the letters wrap round another piece

parts.note: how means the way in which
the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: How a new dictionary dealt with the entry for square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' looks like a dictionary covering a topic, but is a container indicator: way plus new wraps round the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk gathering with square dancing.

clue.text: Summon attendant

definitions.meaning: to call someone by name over a loudspeaker in a hotel or airport
a young servant or boy who runs errands, as at a hotel

explanation.definitionFit: Hotels call guests over the tannoy, and a pageboy is a young attendant.

clue.text: Close relative with fruit

parts.note: papa is father, a close relative

explanation.surface: A near relation has some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A papaw is a tropical fruit, another name for papaya.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing, owe lender, perhaps, a pound

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be otherwise, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, stands for a pound in money

explanation.surface: A layabout owes the moneylender a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OWE LENDER; L is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A ne'er-do-well is an idle, worthless person, a wastrel.

clue.text: Row made by class

definitions.meaning: a line of soldiers or things side by side

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers stand in a rank, a line, and rank also means social grade or standing.

clue.text: One may have a shock, attacked with its teeth

definitions.text: One may have a shock, attacked with its teeth

parts.words: One may have a shock, attacked with its teeth
parts.note: a shock here is a mass of hair, and the attacker is a toothed tool drawn through it

explanation.surface: Someone gets a fright when bitten by an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a fright, but a shock of hair is what this toothed tool attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb has teeth and is used to tame a thick mop of hair.

clue.text: Choose a deep sound? Not from this instrument

indicators.note: sound? hints that the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: choose means pick, a stays as written, and deep means low

explanation.surface: Picking a low note is impossible on this high-pitched instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK A LOW said aloud gives the answer; 'Not from' adds the joke that this tiny high flute cannot give a deep note.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is a small flute, the highest-pitched woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Row about order given for offensive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a row is a din, noise
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A dispute arises over an order given for an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' suggests a military attack, but means foul-smelling or nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul or disgusting, especially in smell.

clue.text: Refined partners taking on lawyer of leftist inclination

parts.note: West and East are partners in bridge, written W and E
LLB, Bachelor of Laws, is a law degree, so a lawyer
red means left-wing

explanation.surface: Elegant business partners hire a left-wing lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' are bridge partners West and East; 'taking on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-bred means well brought up, polished and genteel.

clue.text: Bill suppressing information unknown in this office

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so one piece keeps another inside it

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
gen is British slang for information
in algebra Y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Bill is withholding secret information in this office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is an account; 'unknown' is Y, the algebra symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a business office or bureau providing a service.
